home_title: A trip where nobody feels they lost.
home_lede: A planner for family and group trips. Code does the maths; the language model only writes questions and explanations.
home_accounts_note: Kids and grandma do not need accounts: you add them as profiles and they vote through a link.
how_1_body: One sentence or a recording. The assistant only asks about what changes the plan most.
how_2_body: Want, don't mind or don't want, with a reason in one tap. Also through a link, no account needed.
how_3_body: Code, not the model, picks a plan where nobody drops below the floor. The same input gives the same plan.
proof_title: A chatbot plan sounds good until someone checks it.
proof_visible_body: A day plan with times, prices and a verdict. Tap a place to see who is for it and who is against.
proof_check_body: Paste a plan from any tool and TuttiTrip counts the problems: opening hours, distances, breaks, budget and accommodation requirements.
proof_price_body: Before the host overrides something, they see what it costs everyone else.
proof_settle_body: Code works out who pays whom, with the fewest transfers. An uncertain receipt reading is marked and needs your confirmation.
closing_title: Build a plan that works for everyone.
about_title: In a group, one person usually plans the whole trip.
about_lede: The child wants a theme park, the teenager something with friends, grandma a museum and a rest, and the partner something cheap and close. Chatbot plans sound good but ignore opening hours, distances and the pace of the slowest person.
about_split_1_body: Fairness solver, plan check, prices, accommodation requirements. No language model: the same input gives the same plan.
about_split_2_body: Interview questions, explanations, reading of pasted plans, offers and receipts.
about_split_3_body: Saving to your calendar, opening an accommodation search. It never buys or books anything on its own.
about_inside_plan_body: Every person rates places and code builds a plan where nobody drops below the floor.
about_inside_check_body: Counts the problems in a plan, including one that came from another tool.
about_inside_expenses_body: You log receipts and the settlement comes out with the fewest transfers.

seo_privacy_description: What data TuttiTrip processes, why, where it goes and how to ask for your account to be deleted. Auth0 sign-in, language models, hosting and browser storage.
privacy_lede: What data TuttiTrip processes about you, why, where it goes and how to ask for it to be deleted. No legal jargon.
privacy_scope: TuttiTrip was built at the HackYeah 2026 hackathon in Kraków. This page describes what the app does today.
privacy_who_title: Who is responsible for the service
privacy_who_p1: TuttiTrip is built by the HackYeah-TuttiTripTeam team. For anything about personal data, write to us through the Contact page (linked at the bottom of this page).
privacy_login_p1: You sign in with a Google or Discord account. Auth0 runs the sign-in: it asks Google or Discord to confirm who you are. The passwords of those accounts never reach us.
privacy_login_p2: From Google or Discord, Auth0 hands the app your name, e-mail address and profile picture. We show them in the app so you can see you are signed in. The TuttiTrip server recognises you by your Auth0 account identifier.
privacy_data_intro: What you save in the app goes to the database of our server and is tied to your account:
privacy_data_trips: trips: name, destination, dates and budget,
privacy_data_people: people on a trip: a first name or nickname, age group and vote weight (profiles the organiser creates, not accounts),
privacy_data_prefs: people's preferences: restrictions, diet, interests and what matters to whom,
privacy_data_invites: invitations: a link with a secret code that gives someone access to a trip,
privacy_data_plans: plans and expenses of a trip.
privacy_data_others: The organiser enters data about other people, children included. Enter only what the plan needs, and only with the consent of those people or their guardians. Diet and restrictions can reveal health or beliefs, so give no more than you must.
privacy_demo_p1: The HackYeah jury can enter the app through a special demo link, without signing in with Google or Discord. The link opens an account with sample data. The app exchanges the code from the link for a short-lived access token (valid for about an hour) and removes the code from the address bar. The token and the invitation code stay only in the memory of the browser tab (sessionStorage), so the session survives a page reload and renews itself quietly when the token expires. Signing out or a failed renewal erases both. The demo data is sample data and we may reset it at any time.
privacy_ai_p1: A language model writes the interview questions, the explanations and the plan drafts. Our code does the numbers, times and prices.
privacy_ai_p2: The model receives the content a task needs, for example the destination and the participants' preferences. We use two kinds of provider. OpenRouter passes the request on to a chosen model (currently Google Gemini). A Qwen model runs on the team's own GPU server. Search by meaning relies on a model that runs on our side.
privacy_ai_p3: We do not train our own models on your data. The rules of OpenRouter and of the model providers it forwards requests to are their own.
privacy_hosting_cloudflare: The site and its proxy to the API run on Cloudflare (Workers). Cloudflare handles the traffic, your IP address included, and may keep technical logs. We also pass the IP address on to the backend.
privacy_hosting_backend: The backend and the database run on a server managed by the team, not on an external database provider.
privacy_hosting_auth0: The data of your sign-in account (name, e-mail, picture) is handled by Auth0.
privacy_assets_p1: The photos on the public pages come from Unsplash (Unsplash licence), but we serve them from our own domain, so Unsplash gets no request when you view the page. We credit the authors next to the photos, and the links to Unsplash open only when you click them. The fonts are ours too.
privacy_assets_p2: We use no analytics tools and no ads.
privacy_osm_p1: We fill our catalogue of places (sights, restaurants and the like) with data from OpenStreetMap, fetched through the Nominatim and Overpass services. We send them only the name of a city, no user data.
privacy_osm_p2: © OpenStreetMap contributors. The data is available under the ODbL licence.
privacy_storage_intro: The site sets no cookies of its own. To work, it saves a few things in the browser's storage:
privacy_storage_theme: the chosen theme, light or dark
privacy_storage_auth0: the Auth0 sign-in session, so you do not sign in every time (also in the installed app)
privacy_storage_join: an invitation code while you sign in, 10 minutes at most
privacy_storage_demo: the demo session: an access token and the invitation code for quiet renewal, until the tab is closed
privacy_storage_reload: a marker that the app reloaded after an update
privacy_storage_outro: The app is a PWA, so its files (code, photos, fonts) also sit in the browser's cache. Auth0 may set its own cookies on its own domain. Clearing the site's data in the browser removes all of this.
privacy_rights_title: Your rights and deleting your account
privacy_rights_p1: You can ask for access to your data, for it to be corrected, deleted or restricted. To delete your account together with the trips and profiles you created, write to us through the Contact page and give the name or e-mail of the account you sign in with.
privacy_rights_p2: We keep the data while your account exists or until you ask for deletion. You also have the right to lodge a complaint with the President of the Personal Data Protection Office (UODO) in Poland.
privacy_changes_p1: When what the app does changes, we update this page and the date at the top.
privacy_contact_p1: The HackYeah-TuttiTripTeam team is on GitHub and on the Contact page.
